sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by NanoBiT complementation (LgBiT + HiBiT) and BRET-based kinetic WNT-ligand binding assays in living HEK293A cells; receptor reached the cell surface and bound ligand. WNT-3A-induced β-catenin signalling was not transduced by FZD3 (consistent with prior literature), but this reflects intrinsic signalling selectivity, not a tag-induced defect.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 both report an N-terminal HiBiT tag on full-length, membrane-anchored FZD3 expressed in HEK293A cells, with surface display confirmed by NanoBiT complementation and ligand-binding kinetics. The signal peptide ends at residue 22 (topology landmark), so the tag must be placed after residue 22 to avoid being cleaved; Python confirms residue 22 = G and residue 23 = H. The mature extracellular N-terminus (EC1, residues 23–203) is 181 residues from TM1, providing ample space for a short tag. L1 is the primary grounding clip; L2 provides the functional confirmation. All 10 human FZD paralogues, including FZD3, were engineered with an N-terminal HiBiT tag. The signal peptide of FZD3 spans residues 1–22 (landmarks), so the tag is placed after residue 22 (the last signal-peptide residue), immediately before the mature N-terminus at H23. HiBiT-FZD3 constructs were transiently expressed in HEK293A cells and used in NanoBiT/BRET kinetic binding experiments in living cells, confirming surface display.

sources.claim: In order to establish a nanoluciferase complementation-dependent NanoBiT/BRET binding assay format to study all human FZD paralogues, we generated constructs for all 10 receptors carrying an N-terminal HiBiT tag ( Figure S1A,B ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both ground the same N-terminal HiBiT site on FZD3; L1 is used as the primary supporting_clip_id because it explicitly describes the engineering of the tagged construct, while L2 confirms surface expression and functional use. The position is topology_derived because neither clip names a specific residue number — the junction is uniquely determined by the signal-peptide boundary (residue 22) from the authoritative topology landmarks: an N-terminal tag on a protein with a signal peptide must go after the cleavage site. L3 describes a BRIL domain insertion in intracellular loop 3 (ICL3, residues 396–420) of FZD3 for structural thermostabilisation; this is an intracellular position and does not qualify as a surface tag site. No other ledger lines support additional extracellular sites.

literature_other_positions.note: BRIL domain inserted between ICL3 residues 399 and 412 (both within the intracellular loop 3 span 396–420) for structural thermostabilisation of FZD3; this is a cytoplasmic insertion, not a surface tag site.
